about: The look of the prototype, as names and values, so a screen built in any framework can use them instead of copying the prototype's markup. Every value was read off prototype/parts (the :root block in parts/m/00_head.html, the five macros in prototype/build.py, and the literal colours, sizes and spacings the screens use). The ROLE names are a reading of how each value is used, not names the prototype itself has, except for the ones marked 'prototype name'. Source of truth for tokens.css: run python3 design/make_tokens.py to regenerate it.

accent.note: The prototype does not define --accent in :root. The page's own runtime sets it on the outermost element from a property named accent (parts/m/00_head.html, the first div after </helmet>), and 78 places use var(--accent). A copy of the markup into another app has no accent unless something sets it. tokens.css sets it on :root.

strong.role: text on buttons and the strongest labels

body.role: body text in cards and lists

secondary.role: paragraphs under a title, the most used text colour

muted.role: less important text, still 4.5:1 on white

on_dark.role: text on the dark band and on the accent colour

on_dark_2.role: second line of text on the dark band

faint.role: struck-through ghost words (a word the reference has and a wording lacks)

mono_label.role: text on the small grey code labels ('best without AI')

sunken.role: a quiet area inside a card

hover.role: hover on quiet buttons, menu items and number discs

selected.role: a chosen option (also used with a 2px accent border)

placeholder.role: fill of a dashed 'optional or not built yet' box

label.role: fill of the small grey code labels

bar_track.role: the empty part of a progress bar

divider.role: row dividers inside lists and tables

control.role: edge of every button and input (3:1 against white)

control_quiet.role: edge of a choice card that is not chosen

dashed.role: the dashed edge that means optional or not built yet

choice.role: edge of a choice card that is not chosen (a second grey the prototype also uses)

danger.role: failed, refused, a guard that stopped something

draft.role: the DRAFT bar and notes about drafts

redline.role: defined in the prototype's :root but no screen uses it through var(); the screens write colours out (see status)

ok.role: defined in the prototype's :root but no screen uses it through var(); the screens write colours out (see status)

warn.role: defined in the prototype's :root but no screen uses it through var(); the screens write colours out (see status)

chart.note: Colours of marks in the two charts. Colour is never the only carrier: every mark also has a shape, a pattern or a word beside it. prototype/chart_colours.py checks them for colour blindness.

alone.role: hollow square: in no cluster, nothing similar found

open.role: square: in a cluster and needs a decision

attention.role: hatched square (stripes of #B35A00 and #FFD9A8): needs attention

attention_stripe.role: the light stripe of the hatched square

info_notice_edge.role: edge and icon of a 'comment' notice

sans.role: everything in the interface; section titles are bold sans, never serif

serif.role: requirement wording ONLY, so serif always means 'this is the text being decided about'

font.licence: SIL Open Font License; the three LICENSE-*.txt files sit next to the fonts. Keep them when you copy the fonts.

type.note: Two or three sizes carry nearly everything: 13px and 12px for the interface, 16px, 18px and 30px for titles. Labels are sentence case, not capitals.

radius.note: ctl, chip and panel are the prototype's own variable names (--radius-ctl, --radius-chip, --radius-panel).

space.note: gap and padding values the prototype actually uses; 8, 6 and 12 are the most common gaps, 24 between page sections.

components.caption: font-size:13px;font-weight:600;color:#54626F;
components.note: These five are the prototype's own macros (MAC in prototype/build.py), copied exactly. tokens.css turns them into the classes .rq-card, .rq-caption, .rq-button, .rq-primary and .rq-input.
